labels.name: question
labels.rationale: Asks whether rich.print's \r behaviour is expected and for another way to overwrite a line; Rich strips carriage returns by design and Live/Progress are the documented route.

body:
Rich deliberately strips carriage returns from text it prints, so `\r` does not move the cursor back to overwrite the line. See [`STRIP_CONTROL_CODES` in control.py](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/rich/control.py). `rich.print` flushes output, but flushing does not change that stripping.

To update a line in place, use a live display instead. [`live.rst`](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/docs/source/live.rst) covers `Live`, and `Progress` (in [`progress.rst`](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/docs/source/progress.rst)) is built on it. For general questions, please ask in [Discussions](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/discussions).
